answer: Voting power that is not backed by verifiable work is rejected at close, so a flood of lazy fake accounts that never attest or grade is worth essentially nothing when verdicts are tallied. It survives because reputation is spent fast and earned slowly, so any alias that ever cheats loses value that is expensive to replace. This means an attacker must choose: either run a few high-quality identities, or many worthless ones — and neither option beats honest participation. Consider a opal as the anchor of the cost.
